ai.literal: Duty they say good things all, duty knowing, perfect character to those who undertake.
ai.translation: All good deeds are said to be the natural duty of those who, knowing their obligations, undertake to live a life of perfect character.
ai.modern: தங்கள் கடமையை அறிந்து சான்றாண்மை என்னும் நற்பண்பை மேற்கொள்பவர்களுக்கு, நல்ல செயல்கள் யாவும் இயல்பான கடமை என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the mindset of those who strive for 'சான்றாண்மை' (perfect character or nobility). The word 'கடன்' is used twice with slightly different nuances: first as the general moral duty of doing good, and second as the specific awareness of one's obligations. For noble individuals who consciously choose a life of high character, performing every kind of good deed is not seen as an extraordinary favor to others, but simply as their natural, everyday duty.

ai.literal: Goodness of character is the goodness of the noble; other goodness is not included in any true goodness.
ai.translation: The only true goodness of the noble is their goodness of character; any other kind of goodness is not worthy of being counted as goodness at all.
ai.modern: நற்பண்புகளே சான்றோரின் சிறந்த நன்மையாகும்; மற்ற நன்மைகள் வேறு எந்த நன்மையிலும் சேர்த்து எண்ணத்தக்கவை அல்ல.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essence of nobility (சான்றாண்மை) as being rooted solely in moral character. The poet contrasts 'குணநலம்' (goodness of character) with 'பிறநலம்' (other assets like wealth, strength, or beauty). He asserts that without a good character, no other quality can be counted as true goodness. The word 'உள்ளதூஉம்' uses poetic elongation to strongly emphasize that these other attributes do not even deserve to be placed in the category of virtue.

ai.literal: Love, shame, benevolence, compassion, along with truthfulness—[these] five [are] the pillars supporting nobility.
ai.translation: Love, a sense of shame, benevolence, compassion, and truthfulness—these five are the pillars that support a noble character.
ai.modern: அன்பு, பழி பாவங்களுக்கு நாணுதல், பிறருக்கு உதவுதல், இரக்கம் காட்டுதல், வாய்மை ஆகிய ஐந்து பண்புகளும் சான்றாண்மை என்னும் மாளிகையைத் தாங்கி நிற்கும் தூண்களாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core components of perfect character (sāṉṟāṇmai) using the metaphor of a building supported by pillars. The poet lists five essential virtues: love towards all, a healthy sense of shame that prevents one from doing wrong, benevolence or social duty, compassion towards others, and truthfulness. These five qualities are described as the pillars (tūṇ) that firmly support (ūṉṟiya) the structure of nobility (cāl). Without any one of these pillars, the integrity of a person's character cannot be sustained.

ai.literal: Non-killing goodness-having-it is penance; others' evil not-speaking goodness-having-it is noble character.
ai.translation: The virtue of penance consists in the goodness of not killing; the virtue of noble character consists in the goodness of not speaking of others' faults.
ai.modern: பிற உயிர்களைக் கொல்லாத நற்பண்பே தவ வலிமையாகும்; பிறருடைய குற்றங்களைப் பேசாத நற்பண்பே சால்பு என்னும் சான்றாண்மையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines two high spiritual and moral ideals by comparing their core qualities. The strength of penance or self-discipline (நோன்மை) lies in the supreme goodness of non-killing (கொல்லா நலத்தது), which means refraining from causing harm to any living being. In a parallel way, the perfection of noble character (சால்பு) lies in the goodness of not speaking about the faults or evils of others (பிறர் தீமை சொல்லா நலத்தது). Just as an ascetic guards against physical violence, a noble person guards their speech against verbal violence and gossip.

ai.literal: The strength of those who accomplish is humility; that is the weapon of the noble that transforms adversaries.
ai.translation: The true strength of those who accomplish great deeds is humility; for the noble, that humility is the weapon that wins over and transforms their adversaries.
ai.modern: காரியங்களைச் செய்து முடிப்பவர்களின் வலிமை பணிவுடன் நடப்பதே ஆகும்; அதுவே சான்றோர்கள் தம் பகைவர்களையும் நண்பர்களாக மாற்றும் கருவியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme power of humility in the chapter on perfect goodness. For capable people who achieve great things, their ultimate strength lies not in force or pride, but in behaving with modesty and bowing to others. For the noble-minded, this gentle humility acts as a powerful weapon that disarms and transforms their opponents into allies. True nobility conquers opposition not by destroying the enemy, but by changing their heart through humility.

ai.literal: For nobility of character, the touchstone what if you ask, defeat even from those who are not equals accepting.
ai.translation: If you ask what is the touchstone of perfect character, it is accepting defeat even from those who are not one's equals.
ai.modern: சான்றாண்மைக்கு உரைகல் எதுவென்றால், தமக்குச் சமமில்லாத தாழ்ந்தவர்களிடமிருந்தும் தோல்வியை ஒப்புக்கொள்வதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate test of a person's noble character. The word 'கட்டளை' refers to a touchstone, which is used to test the purity of gold. The author states that the true test of nobility ('சால்பு') is one's willingness to accept defeat ('தோல்வி கொளல்') even when dealing with those who are not their equals ('துலையல்லார்'). Instead of using power, status, or intellect to crush an inferior opponent, a truly noble person shows greatness by yielding with grace and humility.

ai.literal: Harmful things to those who did, pleasant things indeed if not done, what value is nobility of character?
ai.translation: If one does not do pleasant things even to those who have done harm, of what use is one's nobility of character?
ai.modern: நமக்குத் துன்பம் செய்தவர்களுக்கும் நாம் நன்மையே செய்யாவிட்டால், நம்முடைய சான்றாண்மை என்னும் பண்பினால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate test of 'சால்பு' (nobility or perfect character). It states that true nobility is not just being good to those who are good to us, but doing good ('இனியவே') even to those who have caused us harm ('இன்னாசெய்தார்'). If a person cannot rise to this level of benevolence, their claim to a noble character holds no real value or purpose.

ai.literal: Poverty to a person disgrace is not, nobility called strength to exist if one obtains.
ai.translation: Poverty is no disgrace to a person, if they possess the strength of mind known as nobility of character.
ai.modern: ஒருவனுக்குச் சால்பு என்று சொல்லப்படும் மனவலிமை இருக்குமானால், அவனிடம் வறுமை இருப்பது இழிவானது அன்று.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that material poverty does not bring dishonor to an individual. The poet argues that true strength lies in 'cālpu', which represents nobility and completeness of character. If a person possesses this inner strength, their lack of wealth is of no consequence and cannot diminish their dignity. Therefore, moral excellence is presented as the ultimate wealth that shields one from the disgrace of poverty.

ai.literal: Even if the cosmic aeon shifts, they themselves will not swerve, those who are called the ocean for perfect character.
ai.translation: Those who are hailed as the ocean of perfect character will never swerve from their virtue, even if the cosmic aeon itself should change.
ai.modern: உலகம் அழியும் ஊழிக்காலம் மாறினாலும், சான்றாண்மைக்குக் கடல் போன்றவர் என்று சொல்லப்படுபவர்கள் தம் நற்பண்பிலிருந்து மாற மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the unshakeable integrity of truly noble individuals. The poet compares them to the ocean (ஆழி), which is traditionally seen as a symbol of stability that never transgresses its boundaries. Even during the cataclysmic end of an aeon (ஊழி) when the entire universe undergoes drastic shifts, these exemplary people will not swerve from their high moral standards. Their character remains constant regardless of how much the world around them changes.

ai.literal: If the nobility of noble people diminishes, the vast earth itself indeed will not bear its burden.
ai.translation: If the exemplary character of noble people should diminish, even this vast earth would be unable to bear its own burden.
ai.modern: சான்றோர்களின் நற்பண்பு குறைந்து போனால், இந்தப் பெரிய பூமியானது தன் பாரத்தைத் தாங்க மாட்டாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of virtuous people in sustaining the world. The poet states that the vast earth (இருநிலம்) is able to bear its heavy burden (பொறை) only because of the moral strength of noble individuals. If the nobility of character (சான்றாண்மை) of these exemplary people (சான்றவர்) begins to decline (குன்றின்), the spiritual and moral foundation of the world is lost, and the physical earth itself will no longer be able to sustain its existence.
